preamble: The change of the alveolar nasal [n] to the glottal fricative [h] is a rare debuccalization in which the oral closure is lost while glottal friction remains. Its best-documented case is Basque, where Proto-Basque intervocalic *n became h (Michelena's lenition), as in *anate 'duck' > ahate; the Zuberoan (Souletin) dialect preserves traces of the lost nasality as a nasalized h.

examples.note: Intervocalic *n > h (Michelena); Zuberoan keeps the nasality as nasal h
Also with *b- > m- before a nasal

sources: Trask, R. L. (1997). The History of Basque. Routledge. https://doi.org/10.4324/9781315004358
Michelena, L. (1977). Fonética histórica vasca (2nd ed.). Anejos del Anuario del Seminario de Filología Vasca "Julio de Urquijo" 4. Diputación Foral de Guipúzcoa. https://doi.org/10.1387/asju.8531
